data.title: chat /api/file: re-check dot-segment rule after realpath — non-dot symlink can launder a dot directory

data.body:
Found during AS-26 cycle-2 review (qa-priya), recorded non-blocking and deliberately not fixed in that task.

WHAT: readRepoMarkdown (apps/chat/server.js) rejects dot-leading path segments by testing the REQUESTED STRING, before realpath resolution. So a non-dot-named symlink pointing into a dot directory launders it: demonstrated on a scratch root, 'latticelink -> .lattice' served 'latticelink/plans/p.md' with 200. Realpath containment is unaffected — nothing outside the mounted root is reachable — so this is a scope question inside the repo, not an escape.

WHY IT IS LOW SEVERITY, NOT ZERO: the checkout currently contains no symlinks at all (verified by find), and planting one requires repo write access, which already implies more capability than this would grant. No privilege gain today. It matters because AS-26 made the repo root the mount, so the gate is now the sole boundary for what a network-reachable service can read, and 'dot directories are unreachable' is load-bearing prose in apps/chat/README.md.

FIX SHAPE: re-check the segment rule against the RESOLVED path after realpathSync, not only against the request string. Keep the existing string-level check as a cheap pre-filter. Add a test that plants a symlink into a scratch root and asserts 404.

RELATED, from the same review: on macOS the bind mount is case-insensitive so 'readme.md' serves; not a hole (the dot rule and .md check run on the request string before touching the FS, so case can never widen the reachable class) and it vanishes on the Linux deploy target. Mentioned only so the next reader does not re-derive it.

CTO ordering call (board DM msg 323). Rank 4, and the highest-ranked internal-tools item — it outranks AS-27/32/28/33 despite being unglamorous because /api/file is now the sole read boundary for a container that mounts the whole repo read-only, and the dot-segment rule tests the requested string rather than the resolved path. No live exploit (the checkout has no symlinks and planting one needs repo write access), so it does not preempt the product line; but it is small, it is security debt on a boundary we deliberately widened in AS-26, and it should not sit behind cosmetic work. Still unassigned — default implementer agent:developer-marcus per the internal-tools directive when it is pulled.

provenance.reason: board msg 394: chat issues must all ship; security hardening leads the cluster

data.body: Board directive (DM msg 394): all chat issues ship. Cluster order 1/6 — symlink dot-dir laundering is the one open security finding on a surface the board uses daily; it goes first. Assigned marcus, raised to high.

Reassigned Marcus -> Lena. The earlier assignment predates the 2026-09-02 pair hire (record 11 §9.5.3 pre-agrees Lena for this task), and Marcus is on AS-41. Pulled now as lane B of the AS-60 parallel-lanes trial (AS-60 plan §4.1) and on its own merits as cluster item 1/6, the one open security finding on a board-facing surface. Note for the planner: this task has no description — the three comments above are the whole record, and the plan must therefore carry the context a description normally would. Its stated file scope becomes trial-config.json's allowed prefixes for lane B, so it must be explicit and file-level, and must not touch apps/invoicing/ or tools/.

Planned. Fix: one new check 3b in readRepoMarkdown between realpath containment and isFile — real !== join(rootReal, path) 404s byte-identically; i.e. below-root resolution must be the identity. Policy: symlinks below the root are refused entirely (a naive resolved-dot recheck inherits the .lattice exemption and would still serve Priya's latticelink repro; census shows zero symlinks in tree or git history, so nothing legitimate breaks). Above-root symlinks can't false-reject — both comparands share rootReal. Declared trial scope (lane B): prefix apps/chat/, files server.js + test/api.test.js + README.md; disjoint from apps/invoicing/ and tools/. Probes 16->19 + positive control; falsification R1 revert + R2 wrong-policy mutant specified with predicted failing sets.

lanes-trial: lane spawned — lane B, AS-60 T1, fan start 2026-09-02T06:54:38Z. Implementation runs as a sub-agent confined to .worktrees/AS-34; board writes are serialized through the orchestrator (agent:cto-owen) for the duration.

AS-34 implementation complete on `feat/AS-34-symlink-dot-check` (commit bc7a39f). Diff measured: 3 files, +35/−10 (server.js +11/−4, test/api.test.js +14/−0, README.md +10/−6) — net ≈25 lines, inside the plan's ≈30 estimate; `git diff master...feat/AS-34-symlink-dot-check --name-only` is exactly the three §2 files.

The fix is the plan's §3.1 line verbatim — `if (real !== join(rootReal, path)) throw fail();` — inserted between containment and isFile; docblock enumerates 3b between (3) and (4); README caveat block replaced with the §9.1 wording verbatim. Symlink policy as decided in §3.2: refused outright below the root, dot target or not.

Tests: api.test.js 25/25; full `node --test` in apps/chat 194/194 on the branch. Cardinality: probes 16 → 19 (new: `latticelink/plans/task_TEST.md`, `docslink/ok.md`, `alias.md` — appended, no existing literal changed), happy paths 3 → 4 (new positive control `docs/ok.md`, 200 with exact content). Scratch roots via mkdtemp only, torn down after; no existing container touched. Criterion 4's above-root proof rode along: every green run sat behind macOS `/var -> /private/var`.

Falsification, both recipes run in-place with trapped restore (no build step exists, so the stale-mutant-image hazard is vacuous — stated, not skipped):
- R1 (revert the fix): mutation asserted applied (`grep -c 'real !== join'` = 0; `git diff --stat` exactly 1 deletion). Observed failing set: exactly 1 of 25 — the AS-26 gate test, at probe `latticelink/plans/task_TEST.md`, `200 !== 404`. Matches prediction; no wider, no narrower. Trap restored; `git diff --exit-code` clean; re-run 25/25.
- R2 (wrong-policy mutant, §6.R2 block verbatim): asserted applied (`grep -c AS34_MUTANT` = 1, `grep -c 'real !== join'` = 0; stat +5/−1). Observed: exactly 1 of 25 — same test, same probe, `200 !== 404` — i.e. the naive resolved-dot recheck the plan rejects serves the laundering path via the `.lattice` exemption, and the suite tells the two policies apart. Restored, proven clean, re-run 25/25.

Deviations/notes, numbered:
1. The 3b code line carries no trailing comment — R1's perl anchor requires `fail();\n` right after the semicolon. The 3b annotation lives in the adjacent section comment ("// 3. Realpath containment … + 3b. resolved-path equality (AS-34…) + 4. regular file.") and the docblock instead.
2. Docblock/comment wording deliberately avoids the literal substring `real !== join` so it appears exactly once in server.js (the code line) — keeps R1's assert-applied grep valid for future re-runs. Future editors: don't quote that expression in prose in this file.
3. R2's mutation was applied by a scratchpad Node script rather than inline perl (quoting robustness only); mutant text is §6.R2 verbatim, and I added a second assert (`real !== join` count 0) beyond the plan's.
4. README splice keeps the pre-existing "regardless. Until AS-26 …" line intact to avoid rewrap churn in the unchanged tail; leaves one short line mid-paragraph — cosmetic only.

Nothing left undone. Q1 default honored (containment prefix check retained above the equality). compose.yaml, deploy-shape.test.js, public/* untouched. Ready for QA per §5 — reviewer note: criterion 1's "serves 200 on master today" claim is what R1 demonstrates.

lanes-trial: lane returned — lane B completed normally at 2026-09-02T07:02Z, ~8 min after fan start. Breadcrumb above is the implementer's own text, relayed verbatim; the transition below is the orchestrator's.

Review stage: assigning agent:qa-ruben. Implementer was Lena, so implementer != reviewer holds; this is also Ruben's first review at the company and a small, tightly-specified security fix is the right first one. Priya takes AS-41 (Marcus's) next tick — the Priya/Ruben split across the trial pair, per AS-60 plan §6.3.1. Reviews run at WIP=1 under current rules: the lanes carve-out is unshipped and its verdict is qualified, so it is deliberately not being used to fan these reviews.

PASS — 7/7 acceptance criteria met, no defects found. Not implementation-level rework, not plan-level rework. No inline fixes made (§7 says why).

§0 READ ORDER (disclosed per the Review Gate). CLAUDE.md (Review Gate, Review Rework Loop, Git Methodology) -> the plan in full -> the task comment stream from the top, treating comment 1 (qa-priya's AS-26 finding) as the specification -> the diff cold -> the tests as documents -> then I ran everything and recorded my own verdicts. I read the implementer's report (comment 7) LAST, after every number below was already measured on my own. §6 compares the two; nothing material diverged.

§1 CARDINALITY, THEN QUANTIFICATION.
Examined: 3 changed files; 1 commit; 17 test files / 194 tests; 7 acceptance criteria; 7 convention checks; 20 probe cases in a harness I wrote myself, run against 3 server builds (pristine master, branch, R2 mutant) = 60 endpoint observations; 5 full-suite runs; 4 symlink-census queries; 9 master commits since the branch point.
Passed: 7/7 ACs; 7/7 convention checks; 194/194 tests on the branch; 60/60 probe observations matched my prediction; 2/2 falsification recipes red exactly as predicted, neither wider nor narrower.

§2 WHAT I RAN. All inside .worktrees/AS-34 or in scratch dirs under my scratchpad. No running container was touched: asc-chat-server-1 (8347) and asc-invoicing-web-1 (8348) were never contacted; my harness binds 127.0.0.1 on port 0 and closes itself, and every scratch root is mkdtemp + rm -rf.
(a) node --test in apps/chat on the branch: 194 tests, 194 pass, 0 fail.
(b) An independent probe harness of my own (20 cases, a superset of the suite's), booted against a scratch root I built, run twice: once against a pristine `git archive master` copy of apps/chat extracted to scratch, once against the branch. This is the AC verification "against the running code" rather than against the diff's claims.
(c) Falsification recipes R1 and R2 from plan §6, each as one indivisible step (§5).
(d) Symlink census, merge-seam check, trial merge, convention checks.

§3 THE SECURITY QUESTION, ON ITS OWN TERMS. Master vs branch, same 20 cases, same scratch root:
- 8 alias cases served 200 on master and 404 byte-identically on the branch: latticelink/plans/task_TEST.md (Priya's reproduction); deep/nested/plans/task_TEST.md (laundering at depth 2, symlink NOT in first position); rellink/plans/task_TEST.md (relative-target symlink); secretlink/s.md (alias of a NON-exempt dot directory .secret — the direct analogue of the README's own `link -> .git` example; on master it served the string "SECRET DOT CONTENT"); sfile.md (file alias of a file inside a dot dir); docslink/ok.md; alias.md; selflink/README.md (alias of the root itself).
- 12 cases identical on both: 4 happy paths 200 (README.md, personnel/README.md, .lattice/plans/task_TEST.md, docs/ok.md), hardlink.md 200, readme.md 200 (macOS case), escape.md / dir.md / .env.md / personnel/.hidden.md / no-such-file.md 404, big.md 400.
The change is therefore a strict narrowing: nothing went 404 -> 200 anywhere in my matrix. Reasoning the boundary independently: 3b is a pure conjunction added to the accept condition, and equality with a fully-resolved path implies no below-root component is a symlink (a self-resolving symlink is ELOOP, not an escape). With the checkout at zero symlinks (§4), the reachable set is exactly "every .md regular file <=512KB whose spelling passes the string gate" — which is the operator claim in plan §1.1, and it is now true rather than extensionally true. Null bytes and backslashes are already excluded by FILE_PATH_RE, so join() cannot be steered; the charset is ASCII-only so there is no NFC/NFD trap on macOS. No new shared mutable state and no new concurrency surface: the check is pure and per-request.
Plan Q1 (drop the containment prefix check as redundant?) — I evaluated it and I do NOT flag it. Equality does subsume containment, but keeping check 3 above 3b means a future edit weakening one does not silently lose the other. Q1's default is correct; treat it as closed, not open.

§4 DOES ANYTHING LEGITIMATE BREAK? No — verified, not taken from the plan. Symlink census run by me on 2026-09-02: 0 symlinks in the working tree excluding .git; 0 including .worktrees/ (i.e. across the entire span the container bind-mounts); 0 tracked mode-120000 objects on master; no node_modules anywhere. deploy-shape.test.js requires six paths to be reachable (README.md, PHILOSOPHY.md, CLAUDE.md, apps/chat/README.md, .lattice, personnel) — none of them traverses a symlink, and all still serve. The refuse-symlinks policy costs nothing today.

§5 FALSIFICATION — recipes run by me, as one indivisible step each. Backup taken OUTSIDE the scanned tree (sha256 recorded) on top of git + a trap on EXIT; mutate; assert applied; run; trap restores; prove clean; re-run. I ran the FULL 194-test suite under each mutant, not just test/api.test.js, so that a wider failing set could not hide.
R1 (delete the equality line). Assert-applied: guard occurrences 1 -> 0; git diff --stat exactly "1 file changed, 1 deletion(-)"; the removed line echoed. PREDICTED: exactly one test, the AS-26 gate test, at probe latticelink/plans/task_TEST.md, 200 !== 404. OBSERVED: 194 tests, 193 pass, 1 fail — "api: AS-26 — GET /api/file serves allowlisted repo markdown; every probe 404s byte-identically", AssertionError message "latticelink/plans/task_TEST.md", actual 200, expected 404, strictEqual. EXACT match; not wider, not narrower; nothing to classify. Trap fired; git diff --exit-code clean; restored file sha256 identical to the out-of-tree backup; guard count back to 1; re-run 194/194 green.
R2 (wrong-policy mutant — the naive resolved-dot recheck the plan rejects, §6.R2 block verbatim). Assert-applied: AS34_MUTANT count 1, original guard count 0, stat +5/-1. PREDICTED: red at the same test, same probe, because the mutant inherits the first-segment .lattice exemption. OBSERVED: 194 tests, 193 pass, 1 fail — same test, same probe, actual 200 / expected 404. EXACT match. I also ran my 20-case matrix against the mutant: the naive fix closes only 2 of the 8 alias cases (secretlink/s.md and sfile.md) and still serves Priya's original reproduction plus deep/nested, rellink, docslink/ok.md, alias.md and selflink/README.md. So the naive version of this fix would have shipped the reported bug intact, and the suite does tell the two policies apart. Trap fired; git diff --exit-code clean; zero AS34_MUTANT residue; re-run 194/194 green; probe matrix re-run against the restored file, identical to the pre-mutation run (no stale mutant).

§6 PER-AC VERDICT — 7/7.
AC1 laundering probe: PASS. 404 with byte-identical {"error":"No such file."}, confirmed by the suite (probe 17) and independently by my harness. The AC's premise "serves 200 with 'plan body\n' on master today" I verified DIRECTLY against a pristine git-archive of master (200, plan body) — the implementer demonstrated it via R1, which is branch-minus-one-line; same answer, my path is the stronger one.
AC2 policy probes: PASS. docslink/ok.md and alias.md both 404 byte-identical, in dir and file position. I extended with selflink/README.md (alias of the root) — also 404.
AC3 positive control: PASS. docs/ok.md -> 200, content "docs ok\n". The §5.2 404s are the alias's fault alone.
AC4 no regression, no widening: PASS. 194/194 on the branch; all 16 pre-existing probes still 404 byte-identically and all 3 pre-existing happy paths still 200; no case in my matrix moved 404 -> 200. The above-root condition was genuinely exercised, not assumed: my scratch root was /var/folders/... while its realpath is /private/var/folders/..., so root !== realpath(root) was true on every run and all 4 happy paths still served.
AC5 falsification executed: PASS. Both recipes were run by the implementer and the outcomes plus the cardinality line (probes 16->19, happy paths 3->4) are recorded in comment 7. I re-ran both; both reproduced.
AC6 docs: PASS. server.js docblock enumerates 3b in position between (3) and (4) (lines 52-56). README caveat block replaced with the §9.1 wording verbatim. I checked the new prose for truth rather than presence: "a symlink anywhere inside the tree 404s" — true across 5 symlink shapes I planted; the "`link/x.md` where `link -> .git`" example — true (my secretlink probe); "symlinks above the repo root stay irrelevant" — true and empirically exercised; ".git/, .claude/ and .worktrees/ categorically unreachable" — true for symlink aliasing (see R-1 for the one qualification). No under-claim: the sentence that a symlink to a *servable* location also 404s is present, which is what makes a future legitimate symlink diagnosable in seconds.
AC7 scope clean: PASS. node --test green in apps/chat on the branch; git diff master...feat/AS-34-symlink-dot-check --name-only is exactly the three §2 files — equal to the declared set, not merely a subset.

§7 DIFFERENCES FROM THE IMPLEMENTER'S REPORT (read last). Every number in comment 7 reproduced against my own measurements: diff 3 files +35/-10 with the same per-file split; api.test.js 25/25; full suite 194/194; both recipes failing-set exactly 1 at the same probe with 200 !== 404. Three notes, none of them findings against the work:
(a) Method, in my favour to record: the implementer ran only test/api.test.js under both mutants (1 of 25). I ran all 17 files / 194 tests under both (1 of 194). Same conclusion, wider net — no additional test flipped, so the narrower run concealed nothing. Worth knowing for the next mutation run: a mutant that also broke, say, deploy-shape.test.js would have been invisible at the narrower scope.
(b) Their reviewer note says AC1's "serves 200 on master today" is what R1 demonstrates. Strictly R1 demonstrates branch-minus-the-line, not master; the inference is sound because the diff is confined, but I closed it directly against a git-archive of master instead of inferring it.
(c) Their note 4 self-discloses the short mid-paragraph line in README.md as a deliberate tradeoff to avoid rewrap churn in the unchanged tail. I spotted the same artifact before reading the report and independently reached the same conclusion — see §8.

§8 INLINE FIXES: NONE. The only candidate was the short line at apps/chat/README.md:135. Fixing it either just moves the short line one line down (no gain) or rewraps unchanged prose through line 141 (churn in text this task did not touch). The implementer disclosed the tradeoff and gave a real reason; I concur and left it. No typos or defects were found elsewhere in the diff.

§9 CONVENTION CHECKS — 7/7 pass, nothing to route.
C1 commit message "AS-34: refuse in-repo symlinks in /api/file — resolved path must equal requested path" matches AS-<n>: <imperative summary>.
C2 identity: author AND committer both developer-lena <developer-lena@agents.american-software.local> — the actor-id form settled 2026-09-01.
C3 no board state on the branch: git diff master...branch --name-only -- .lattice is 0 files.
C4 declared scope honoured: exactly apps/chat/server.js, apps/chat/test/api.test.js, apps/chat/README.md — all under the §2 allowed prefix apps/chat/; no writes under apps/invoicing/, tools/, docs/, top-level *.md or .lattice/. Lane-B disjointness evidence holds.
C5 protected top-level files untouched: the edited README is apps/chat/README.md (app doc, explicitly implementer-editable per §9.1), not root README.md / CLAUDE.md / PHILOSOPHY.md / agents.md. compose.yaml, deploy-shape.test.js and public/* untouched as §1.3 required.
C6 authorship relay preserved: comment 7 carries actor agent:developer-lena while the lanes-trial instrumentation carries agent:cto-owen. The relay kept the implementer's authorship distinct from the orchestrator's markers; no blending.
C7 merge seam: 9 master commits since the branch point at 299e67f, all .lattice/ board state, none touching apps/chat/. git merge-tree produces 0 conflict markers. Worktree clean, one commit, no untracked files.

§10 RESIDUALS — recorded so nobody re-derives them. Neither is a defect and neither is part of the verdict.
R-1 (routed to the plan owner, agent:cto-owen, as an optional one-sentence follow-up): hard links are outside the policy, and read strictly, "categorically unreachable regardless of how the tree is aliased" over-claims by one alias mechanism. Reproduction: hardlink.md hard-linked to .lattice/plans/task_TEST.md serves 200 on master AND on the branch — realpathSync does not dereference hard links, so real === join(rootReal, path) holds. Why this is NOT a defect and NOT a blocker: it is outside every stated AC; it needs local filesystem write access to the checkout, and anyone with that can simply copy the file to a servable path, so it grants no capability — the same argument that made the original finding low severity; git cannot represent hard links, so one cannot arrive via clone/pull/checkout; and the fix strictly narrows the reachable set either way. The concrete shape if anyone wants the sentence tightened: .claude/ does contain .md files (.claude/commands/advance.md, .claude/agents/*.md).
R-2: the README's earlier summary at apps/chat/README.md:108-110 enumerates the gate as "strict charset, segment rules, realpath-prefix containment, regular file, 512 KB cap" and does not mention 3b. Not false in context — the very next paragraph adds it — and outside §9.1's declared scope, so I deliberately did not expand the diff to touch it. Offered to the plan owner as an optional one-clause addition.

VERDICT: PASS. 7/7 acceptance criteria, 7/7 convention checks, 194/194 tests, both falsification recipes red exactly as predicted and green after restore, both trees clean. The boundary holds and the policy the plan chose is the policy the code implements — R2 proves the suite would have caught the naive alternative. Recording only; the orchestrator transitions and merges.
